Guided solution path 1 · C8 · Level 3

The Variable Is a Waypoint

1

Name the Sunday-sized unit

Let be Sunday ticket sales. Then Saturday sales are ; .
2

Recover the hidden unit

Combine like terms, then divide by the number of equal groups. Write on your paper.
3

Translate to the requested day

Friday is one fifth of Sunday. What operation takes the Sunday quantity to Friday? Record your final quantity and units yourself.
The checkpoint
If you stop as soon as the variable is found, whose tickets have you reported? Why does each equal box represent Sunday—not Friday?
Guided solution path 2 · C9 · Level 4

Grow the Sides, Then Compare

1

Turn changes into multipliers

Set and . Calculate both areas yourself.
2

Compare like quantities

First find . The old area is the comparison base. Why is the new area not the denominator?
3

Name the percent, not the area

Use . Carry out the final arithmetic and enter only the requested percent value.
A useful mental picture
Two growth machines act on two dimensions. Why does multiplying the two side factors capture a corner of extra area that adding the percentages misses?
Guided solution path 3 · C10 · Level 4

A Negative Division Turns Both Signs

1

Keep all three parts together

Subtract throughout: . Which endpoint is strict?
2

Reverse both comparisons

Divide every part by . Write the bounds yourself, then reorder so smaller numbers appear on the left.
3

Test the boundary decisions

Substitute each boundary into the original inequality. Choose open or closed circles; test an interior value and a value outside.
Why the mirror happens
Multiplying by a negative reflects order on the number line. Which original comparison determines each endpoint after the order reverses?
0:23–0:26 · Three-minute reset

Reset Your Attention

Minute 1

Stand up. Relax your hands and shoulders. Look away from the screen.

Minute 2

Get water. Walk or stretch comfortably. Leave the previous item behind.

Minute 3

Sit down. Put the scratch paper in order. Say: “Next item, fresh setup.”
Return with one routine
Define → relate → solve → target. Your last check belongs before the commit button.
TEI mechanics 1 · Level 2 · 1:15

Type the Quantity, Not the Unit

M1Level 2Numeric entry
A printer has already printed pages. Each additional cartridge prints pages. What is the minimum number of additional cartridges needed to print at least pages altogether?
Enter a number only. Keep units out of the response field.
Capacity is a staircase
What remains after the pages already printed? If the quotient is not a whole number, would rounding down meet “at least”?
Entry audit
Read the requested format first. For this field: no units, no commas, no sentence. The real exam may provide an equation editor.
TEI mechanics 2 · Level 2 · 1:15

One Click Is Not a Complete Set

M2Level 2Multiple response
Select all expressions equal to of a positive number .
Select all that apply.
Translate the percent symbol
Percent means “per hundred.” What happens when the given percent is already less than ?

Selection audit

Read every option. Explain a reason to include or exclude each. A highlighted choice records a selection, not correctness.
TEI mechanics 3 · Level 3 · 1:15

The Base Changes at Each Stage

M3Level 3Drag and drop
An item starts at price . A discount is applied, then an surcharge is applied to the discounted price. Place an expression at each stage.
Starting price
After discount
After surcharge

Drag a label into a row, or select a label then click a row. Two labels are unused.

Use an assembly line
At each station, ask: “What quantity is entering this machine?” Is the surcharge based on the original price or the discounted price?

Placement audit

Read the row label after dropping. To revise, choose another token and place it in that row. Selection is not a correctness signal.
TEI mechanics 4 · Level 2 · 1:15

Place a Point, Then Read It Back

Plot one point. Click an intersection; click another to replace it.
Mouse or coordinate menus both work. One blue point is your current selection.
M4Level 2Point graph
Point A is at . Plot its reflection across the -axis.
Which distance stays the same?
A reflection across a vertical line changes left–right position. How can the point keep its distance from the y-axis without changing height?

0:54–0:56 · Exit transfer · Level 3

Can the Next Item Fool You?

E1Level 3Numeric entry
A machine has already filled bottles. It then fills bottles each minute. What is the least whole number of additional minutes needed to have at least filled bottles altogether?
Enter a number only. Keep units out of the response field.
Defend your interpretation
Why does one fewer minute fail? What are you counting: bottles still needed, all bottles, or additional minutes? If one more bottle is requested, must the whole-minute result always change?
